criteria.notes: Two anti-vacuity findings a reader must have, both recorded rather than papered over. (a) DROPPED BEARER — the second fast-check property, 'no random walk of any length ever lands on promoted without passing through dev_eval, held_out_eval, shadow_run, and independent_review in that order' (state-machine.test.ts:95-122), is VACUOUS IN PRACTICE and is deliberately NOT cited above. Its assertions live inside `if (current === "promoted")` (:109). A uniform-random walk of length <= 12 over 11 states, where an illegal step is skipped without advancing, reaches `promoted` only by drawing the correct next state 7 times in the right order while never drawing an absorbing state — measured probability ~1.8e-6 per case. Re-running the test's own loop and arbitraries under fast-check for 50,000 cases (10x its own 5,000) entered the body ZERO times (closeout-c1b transcript). The zero is SEED-DEPENDENT and should not be read as an impossibility proof — a reviewer's independent 50,000-case run entered it ONCE, and derived ~1.6e-6/case analytically, agreeing with the figure above. The argument does not rest on the zero: at that rate a 5,000-case CI run enters the body about 0.008 times, so on the overwhelming majority of executions — including both cited CI runs — the property asserts nothing at all. The test passes, is green in both cited CI jobs, and asserts nothing about ordering. It is a strictly weaker restatement of what the table's shape (citation state-machine.ts:52) already guarantees structurally, so nothing is lost by not citing it — but a reader should not count it. Not fixed here, per the pass rule against fixing findings in the same pass. (b) SHARED ORACLE — the 121-case 11x11 loop (:19-30) and the 10k property (:81-93) both compute their expectation as `LEARNING_PROPOSAL_TRANSITIONS[from].includes(to)`, i.e. from the very table the function under test is constructed from (state-machine.ts:67-70). They therefore prove `createTransitionFn` conforms to its table — a real property, and the one the criterion's 'finds no illegal path' literally asks for — but they cannot detect a WRONG table. The three citations that can are :32 (four hardcoded skip shapes), :15 (11 keys pinned against 02's own union) and :56 (absorbing set pinned against a separately-written constant). Third, on the channel: the criterion names 'CI job + fast-check report'. There is no separate committed fast-check report artifact in this repository, and none is produced by any workflow; the `learning-redteam` job log's per-`it()` lines 232-233 (with the run counts visible in source at :91 `{ numRuns: 10_000 }` and :120 `{ numRuns: 5_000 }`) are the report, and the scoped verbose transcript reproduces them locally. Flagged so the wording is not read as pointing at a missing file. (d) CITATION RE-RESOLUTION. This record was written at base `eabb65a` and re-resolved against `origin/main` as of `f05970c` (provenance rots within minutes, so read this as 'as of', and re-run the diff at merge time). The proof is scoped to THE PATHS THIS RECORD CITES, not to whole packages — a package-level claim was true at `30f931e` and had already rotted by `f05970c`, when `2ea3689` touched `packages/cli`. `git diff eabb65a f05970c -- <the 19 distinct paths cited by this record>` is EMPTY, so all 32 in-repo `test`/`artifact` citations point at byte-identical files. The 19 paths are enumerable from this record itself: every `citations[].ref` of kind `test` or `artifact` whose path is not under `docs/evidence/phase-22/`. A resolver extracted 77 code-shaped snippets from those citations and located all 77 within their cited spans, 0 slid, 0 not found, 0 citations yielding zero snippets. criteria.notes: Scope, stated so this tick is not read wider than the evidence. (a) The phase's own evidence README is explicit that the meetable claim is the CLI/MCP-tool boundary, not arbitrary in-process code execution: docs/evidence/phase-22/README.md 'Threat model, precisely' records that the pre-repair-pass doc's 'structurally incapable' wording was FALSE, because code with arbitrary in-process rights can always supply its own hostile `verify`. This closeout agrees and does not re-import the retracted claim. What is proven: a caller-supplied claim of prior verification is insufficient — some verification must genuinely run and genuinely succeed, twice, with distinct results — plus, separately, that no model-invokable route to this code exists at all. (b) The red-team suite injects a decoupled reference verifier, not the production one; the production verifier (`buildLearningReviewTokenVerifier`, packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.ts:73) is exercised by packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.test.ts, cited under criterion 4. Oracle and subject are therefore genuinely separate here — the oracle is test-support code, the subject is ProposalRegistry's accumulate-then-require-two logic — which is what makes the flagship case non-circular. (c) 'two distinct approval tokens' does NOT mean two distinct human identities; the same operator running `learn approve` twice satisfies it. Disclosed in the phase README's threat-model section and repeated here so the tick is not read as a two-person rule. (d) Measured by this pass for the scan's anti-vacuity floor: packages/gateway/src contains 73 TypeScript files, so the glob the two scans walk is real and large even though the committed floor only requires more than one. (e) DROPPED BEARERS — two tests that look like the most direct evidence for THIS criterion's invariant are vacuous and are deliberately not cited. `registry.test.ts:271-281` ('TransitionOptions carries NO reviewApprovals field at all — a caller cannot supply a trusted-by-name approvals array to transition()') and `promote.test.ts:91-98` (the same for `PromoteProposalOptions`) each declare an object literal with two or three fields and then assert `expect(Object.keys(options)).not.toContain("reviewApprovals")` — on the literal they wrote one line earlier. That is a tautology: `Object.keys` of a literal cannot contain a key the literal does not spell, whatever the TYPE says. Their shared doc comment claims the compile step covers it — 'this file would fail to compile if `TransitionOptions` still declared `reviewApprovals`' — and that claim is FALSE, because an OPTIONAL field is satisfied by omitting it. This pass measured it rather than reasoning about it: putting `readonly reviewApprovals?: readonly { readonly tokenId: string }[]` back on both interfaces leaves `npx tsc -b --force packages/contracts packages/journal packages/learning` at exit 0 AND leaves both tests passing (`docs/evidence/phase-22/closeout-c3b-type-level-proof-probe.txt`; both edits reverted, `git status --porcelain -- packages/` empty at the closeout commit). So neither test constrains the removal it is named for. The invariant itself IS genuinely evidenced — by the flagship fabrication case, the confused-deputy/wrong-subject/replay cases, the positive control, and `registry.test.ts:308-328`'s distinctness backstop, all cited above — which is why this criterion is still ticked. Recorded, not fixed: the honest repair is to make the field's absence a compile ERROR (e.g. an `Exclude<keyof TransitionOptions, …>` assertion or a `@ts-expect-error` on a literal that supplies it), and that is separate work with its own TDD trail.

citations.quotedAssertion: job log line 202 — '  ✓  @crabgic/learning  src/red-team/grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts (6 tests) 30ms'. Also green on ubuntu-24.04-arm (job 91480517035) in the same run, which matters for a test whose whole subject is real POSIX mode bits.

packages/learning/src/red-team/grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts:53-58 — the POSITIVE control the test's own name calls out ('sanity — the boundary isn't vacuously "always fails"'): before sealing, 'await store.write([evalCase]);' / 'expect(await store.read()).toEqual([evalCase]);'. Without it, a store whose write always failed would satisfy every EACCES assertion below.

packages/learning/src/red-team/grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts:60-69 — the fs-permission proof, deliberately bypassing every abstraction this package offers: 'await expect(' / 'writeFile(join(heldOutDir, "tamper.json"), JSON.stringify({ hacked: true }), "utf8"),' / ').rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "EACCES" });' after store.seal(). :71-80 repeats it for OVERWRITING the existing sealed cases file (the case a directory-mode-only seal would miss), and :91-98 proves reads still succeed, so the seal is write-only and not a blanket lockout.

packages/learning/src/store/case-fixture-store.ts:65-72 — what makes the boundary OS-level rather than a convention: 'async seal(): Promise<void> {' / 'await chmod(join(this.#dir, name), LEARNING_SEALED_FILE_MODE);' / 'await chmod(this.#dir, LEARNING_SEALED_DIR_MODE);'. Modes pinned at store/layout.ts:47-50 as 0o500 / 0o400. :47-50's in-process refusal ('is sealed — refusing write', :49) is the weaker, layered companion — the EACCES above holds without it.

packages/learning/src/red-team/grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts:100-112 — the disjointness half: 'expect(heldOutStore.isSealed).toBe(true);' / 'expect(devStore.isSealed).toBe(false);' and the dev store then genuinely written twice over, 'expect(await devStore.read()).toHaveLength(2);'. Sealing one namespace does not seize the other.

packages/learning/src/store/layout.test.ts:28-34 — the paths the criterion names really are disjoint namespaces under 04's pinned root: 'expect(devDir).not.toBe(heldOutDir);' / 'expect(devDir.startsWith(resolveGraderDir(env, projectHash))).toBe(true);' / 'expect(heldOutDir.startsWith(resolveGraderDir(env, projectHash))).toBe(true);'. :20-26 does the same for registry/ versus grader/.

packages/learning/src/store/layout.test.ts:14-18 — the state root pinned as a literal, not re-derived: 'expect(resolveLearningDir(env, projectHash)).toBe(' / '"/home/tester/.local/state/crabgic/abc123/learning",'. That is roadmap/22 §In scope's storage-policy path (XDG state home, crabgic, project hash, learning) reproduced exactly, and the sibling convention interface-ledger Gap 14 settles.

packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.ts:139-145 — the structural half the phase README calls a type-level absence: the ProposalRegistry constructor takes 'readonly journal: Pick<JournalStore, "appendEntry">;' and a registryDir, and no grader/held-out path at all. Cited as source rather than as a test because that is what it is — there is no runtime check here to be bypassed, and equally no test asserting the absence.

'Test Files  2 passed (2)' / '      Tests  9 passed (9)' — scoped local re-run of grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts plus layout.test.ts at the closeout base commit, --reporter=verbose. Run on Linux, where the 0o500/0o400 seal is genuinely enforced by the kernel for a non-root uid.

criteria.notes: Three residuals, named rather than papered over, because this tick is narrower than its headline sentence. (i) Only `grader/held-out/` is ever sealed. `grader/dev/` (layout.ts:65-67) has no seal step, so nothing stops a same-uid process writing dev cases; the criterion's 'grader/held-out paths' is evidenced for the held-out half and, for the grader half, only by the disjoint-namespace and type-level-absence arguments above. (ii) NO PRODUCTION CALLER EVER SEALS. `git grep 'CaseFixtureStore' packages --include=*.ts`, outside tests, hits only its own definition and the barrel export (index.ts:59); packages/cli/src/bootstrap.ts wires ProposalRegistry and resolveRegistryDir and nothing else from this package's store layer. So the OS boundary this criterion cites is real and proven, and in the shipped binary it is never established, because the grader directories are never created by shipped code at all. The criterion's words are about the test, and the test delivers; the deployment gap is recorded here so no reader infers it. (iii) The test operates on an mkdtemp directory named 'held-out', not on resolveHeldOutCasesDir's output — the pinned path is asserted separately (layout.test.ts:28-34) and the two are never composed. Also, two stale doc comments found while reading: store/layout.ts:33 and store/case-fixture-store.ts:33 both point at a `grader-isolation.test.ts` under src/store/ (the file is src/red-team/grader-isolation.redteam.test.ts), and layout.ts:38-39 names `../store/grader-store.ts` and `../proposal-store/proposer-store.ts`, neither of which exists at HEAD. Left unedited per the pass rule against fixing findings in the same pass.

criteria.text: `learn list|approve|reject|rollback` passes P09's CLI conformance harness, replacing its `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` stub (golden CLI-output test).

citations.quotedAssertion: packages/cli/src/commands/learn-dispatch.test.ts — the suite that did not exist, mirroring phase 12's ticked trust-dispatch.test.ts precedent including its control shape. It drives each of the four verbs through the real dispatchCommand to the real backend, and :191 — 'CONTROL: still returns the typed NOT_IMPLEMENTED shape for all four when deps.learning is absent' — is the control that makes routing, rather than the backend, what changed the outcome.

The seam probe that IS this criterion's redness. Un-wiring each verb ONE AT A TIME — replacing the whole ternary with an unconditional not-implemented result, exactly as a shipped CLI missing its composition-root wiring would behave — left 119 files and 1398 tests green at the base commit, four times over. After the new suite lands, each un-wiring reddens 1 or 2 cases, while learn-command-backend.test.ts stays green throughout because it bypasses the dispatcher, which is precisely the seam this defect named. The transcript also records a correction to the plan it executed: inverting the condition instead of un-wiring measures the WRONG direction and would have produced a red run labelled as the criterion's green redness.

The golden CLI-output test the criterion's parenthetical names: `learn list --json` for an empty registry and for one proposal. Proven load-bearing rather than decorative — adding a key to the payload reddens both snapshot cases while the backend suite's toMatchObject stays green, and renaming the key reddens all three.

criteria.notes: Left unticked. The backend is real and well-tested and the shipped composition root wires it (bootstrap.ts:307-309, asserted by e2e/live/src/cliNotImplementedSweep.test.ts:105 'expect(wiring.learningWired).toBe(true);' — an offline test, re-run for this pass as docs/evidence/phase-22/closeout-c6b-production-wiring.txt). But both channels the criterion names are unsatisfied. P09 identifies its conformance harness by suite name in its own exit criterion 1 — 'Every plan CLI command exists as a typed UDS request with stable exit codes; `--json` validates against published schemas — suite `cli.commands.schema.test`' (roadmap/09-cli-and-doctor.md, quoted rather than line-referenced on purpose: another phase's roadmap renumbers every time its own closeout lands, and this one already moved twice while this record was being written); in packages/cli/src/commands/cli.commands.schema.test.ts the four learn verbs appear on exactly four lines, :224-227, all inside describe('dispatchCommand — NOT_IMPLEMENTED stubs') asserting EXIT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED — the harness records the stub as still present. And there is no golden CLI-output test of the verbs: `grep -c 'toMatchSnapshot|toMatchFileSnapshot' packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.test.ts` is 0, and the only committed golden naming learn is its HELP topic (cli.snapshots.test.ts.snap:174-176). Compounding both: unlike phase 12's analogous trust criterion, which had trust-dispatch.test.ts driving the real dispatchCommand, there is no learn-dispatch.test.ts — dispatch.ts:112-125's four wired branches are never executed by any test. Search trail captured verbatim in docs/evidence/phase-22/closeout-c6-cli-conformance-search-trail.txt. **Remediated 2026-08-07 (closeout batch G).** All three conjuncts now have bearers (PR #115), following phase 12's ticked trust precedent exactly. CORRECTION TO THIS RECORD'S OWN TEXT, measured 2026-08-07 rather than assumed: the four learn verbs have NOT left the NOT_IMPLEMENTED stubs describe in cli.commands.schema.test — they are still in it, and that is deliberate. That suite supplies no deps.learning, and install, run, approve, the connection verbs and the trust verbs sit in the same it.each list while carrying ticked criteria of their own; the deps-absent row is the CONTROL, exactly as roadmap/12's ticked box records for trust. Reading a row in that list as evidence that a verb is unwired would untick phase 12's box too. What changed is that dispatch.ts's four wired arms, which no test executed at all, are now driven end to end with a per-verb un-wiring probe behind each.

criteria.text: Every `learning_transition` journal entry round-trips through 02's `JournalEntryType` exhaustiveness compile check (shared CI job with 02/04).

citations.ref: CI / typecheck (ubuntu-latest), job 91480519764, steps "tsc -b (cold)" and "tsc -b (incremental, no-op expected)"
citations.quotedAssertion: job log lines 158-164 — '##[group]Run npm run typecheck' / 'npm run typecheck' / '> crabgic-monorepo@0.0.0 typecheck' / '> tsc -b', repeated at lines 166-172 for the incremental pass, both green. This IS the shared-CI-job-with-02/04 the criterion names: one whole-monorepo `tsc -b` compiles packages/contracts, packages/journal and packages/learning in the same job, and it is the only job that evaluates either exhaustiveness Record.

packages/journal/src/codec/journal-payloads.ts:203-217 — the exhaustiveness mechanism itself, with this phase's member in it: 'export const JOURNAL_ENTRY_PAYLOAD_SCHEMAS = {' … 'learning_transition: LearningTransitionPayloadSchema,' … '} satisfies Record<JournalEntryType, z.ZodTypeAny>;'. The `satisfies` is the check: omitting learning_transition, or adding a key 02 never declared, fails `tsc -b packages/journal`. Note for accuracy: this object has NO runtime consumer anywhere — searching packages/journal and packages/contracts for its name, outside its own declaration and tests, returns nothing — so it is purely a compile-time assertion, which is exactly what the criterion calls it.

packages/contracts/src/journal/journal-entry-type.ts:79 — 'learning_transition: "A LearningProposalState transition (22).",' inside JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPE_DESCRIPTIONS, the Readonly<Record<JournalEntryType, string>> that is 02's own half of the same mechanism, with the member declared in the union at :38. Given its own citation rather than quoted inside the journal one, so the drift check on each file is separately auditable.

packages/journal/src/codec/journal-entry.ts:162-168 — the RUNTIME half that makes 'round-trips' literal rather than metaphorical: 'export const LearningTransitionEntrySchema = z' / '.object({' / '...envelopeFields,' / 'type: z.literal("learning_transition"),' / 'payload: LearningTransitionPayloadSchema,' / '})' / '.strict();', a branch of the 13-member 'export const JournalEntrySchema = z.discriminatedUnion("type", [' at :171. `.strict()` means an unexpected payload key is a parse error, not a silent pass-through.

packages/journal/src/store/append-entry.ts:141 — the WRITE side of the round trip: 'const entry = JournalEntrySchema.parse({ ...draft, hash });'. Every append goes through it, so an entry that did not validate against the strict discriminated union could not be written at all.

packages/journal/src/codec/ndjson-codec.ts:28 — the READ side, against the same union: 'return JournalEntrySchema.parse(parsed);'. Given its own citation rather than quoted inside the append-entry one, so each file's drift is separately checkable. Together these two are what make 'round-trips' literal.

packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.ts:285-289 — this phase's only writer: 'await this.#journal.appendEntry({' / 'type: "learning_transition",' / 'workUnitId: id,' / 'payload: { from, to },' / '});' — through @crabgic/journal's typed appendEntry, never a hand-rolled envelope, so it cannot skip the parse at append-entry.ts:141.

packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.test.ts:107-121 — the round trip executed end to end against a real store: after one real transition, 'expect(entries).toHaveLength(1);' and 'expect(entries[0]).toMatchObject({' / 'type: "learning_transition",' / 'workUnitId: proposal.id,' / 'payload: { from: "observation", to: "reproducer" },' / '});'. :123-135 is the negative control — an illegal transition 'journals nothing' ('expect(entries).toHaveLength(0);'), so the writer is not simply emitting an entry for every call.

'# command: npx tsc -b --force packages/contracts packages/journal packages/learning' / '# exit status: 0' — a COLD (--force) rebuild for this closeout, so both compile-time Records were genuinely re-evaluated rather than served from an incremental build cache.
'Test Files  2 passed (2)' / '      Tests  63 passed (63)' — scoped local re-run of registry.test.ts plus @crabgic/journal's own journal-entry.test.ts at the closeout base commit.

criteria.notes: Two precisions. (a) WHO WRITES. `learning_transition` entries are appended by packages/learning/src/proposal-store/registry.ts:285 running inside the CLI process (`learn approve`/`reject`/`rollback` via packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.ts), NOT by the supervisor daemon. That makes this package one of the direct journal writers named in the writer-separation disclosure. This criterion makes no claim about writer identity, so nothing here is affected — but a reader should not infer daemon-mediated writes from the word 'journal'. (b) The criterion's phrase '02's `JournalEntryType` exhaustiveness compile check' names one thing that is physically two, in two packages: 02's Readonly<Record<JournalEntryType, string>> descriptor (contracts, cited above) and 04's `satisfies Record<JournalEntryType, z.ZodTypeAny>` payload map (journal, cited above). Both are pure `tsc -b` assertions with no runtime consumer; the runtime round trip is a separate mechanism (JournalEntrySchema's strict discriminated union). All three are cited so the tick does not rest on conflating them. Unlike packages/git-engine, packages/learning carries no compliance test of its own asserting that this package's entry types are a subset of JOURNAL_ENTRY_TYPES; there is exactly one type it writes, it is a string literal at registry.ts:286 checked by the appendEntry parameter type, and the round trip at registry.test.ts:107-121 exercises it — but a reviewer wanting git-engine's belt-and-braces shape should know it is absent here.

criteria.text: Project-scoped promotion produces a real `ChangeSet` that clears the same gates (14) as any other change before publish (08) — integration test on fake engine proves no bypass path exists.
criteria.notes: Left unticked. The first clause is genuinely and non-vacuously evidenced: no-bypass.redteam.test.ts:99-128 constructs @crabgic/gates' own createGateRegistry(), registers one passing and one FAILING fake gate, fires both against the promoted ChangeSet's id, and asserts the failing one really reports false and that two evidence_pointer entries are journaled under that changeSetId — an implementation that special-cased learning-originated ChangeSets into always-green fails :118. What is not evidenced are the clauses after the em dash. There is no engine in the 'integration test on fake engine' (git grep 'FakeEngineAdapter|@crabgic/testkit' over that file returns nothing; the fake engine is in pipeline.e2e.test.ts, which fires no gates). 'Proves no bypass path exists' rests on a doc-comment grep at no-bypass.redteam.test.ts:28-30, not on a check; this pass re-ran it independently and it is true today, but nothing enforces it — contrast phase 07's spawn-surface-scan.test.ts, which turns exactly this kind of absence claim into a permanent static check. And 'before publish (08)' is exercised nowhere: packages/cli/src/learning/learn-command-backend.ts:191-201 is the only production caller of promoteProposal, and it constructs the ChangeSet, prints it to stdout and returns — nothing persists or dispatches it, so in the shipped system a promoted lesson's ChangeSet never reaches gates or publish at all. The honest correction ('a promoted ChangeSet is not special-cased when gates are fired against it') is strictly WEAKER than the criterion, which per the wording protocol makes this UNMET rather than a wording fix. Search trail captured verbatim in docs/evidence/phase-22/closeout-c8-no-bypass-search-trail.txt. **Partially remediated 2026-08-07 (closeout batch G) — the box stays UNTICKED, and the WORDING-MISMATCH route was considered and DECLINED.** PR #115 closed the two clauses that were bookkeeping. The integration test on fake engine now exists: pipeline.e2e.test.ts, which already runs entirely on the fake engine adapter, gained a gate-firing beat appended after its last cited line through a dynamic import, so every line this record cites stays byte-stable; that beat binds to the GENUINE gates registry, measured by green-lighting the registry's own fireOne and watching the beat redden alongside no-bypass.redteam.test.ts after a rebuild, where the src-only leg had under-reported the blast radius to zero. And proves no bypass path exists is no longer a doc-comment grep: no-gate-bypass-surface.redteam.test.ts enforces it statically in the spawn-surface-scan idiom this record's own remedy named, with an anti-vacuity floor and a directory-resolves guard, and planting one importing file reddens that case and only that case. The stronger form, banning the gates import outright, was written, measured and rejected because the eval runner legitimately imports findEvidenceForRequirement, which this phase's In scope requires. WHAT STILL BLOCKS THE TICK: before publish (08) is unexercised — learn-command-backend.ts is still the only production caller of promoteProposal and it constructs the ChangeSet, prints it and returns. This pass declined the wording route for two measured reasons rather than one. First, this phase's Out of scope says a promoted lesson only constructs and HANDS OFF a ChangeSet, and the hand-off does not happen either, so a criterion reworded to say hands off would not be borne by the code any more than the original is. Second, this record's own remedy option (b) requires the reword to land in its own reviewed commit, not by a closeout pass, which is what this pass is. The gap is now exactly one clause wide and its disposition is an owner ruling: remedy (a) persist the promoted ChangeSet into the durable registry, or remedy (b) reword in a reviewed commit.
